items.title: ‘RuPaul’s Drag Race’ Renewed For Season 19 At MTV & Paramount+ Picks Up ‘RuPaul’s Drag Race All-Stars’ For Season 12
items.summary:
MTV has renewed RuPaul's Drag Race for a 19th season, and Paramount+ has ordered a 12th season of RuPaul's Drag Race All Stars. Both pickups include the shows' respective aftershows, RuPaul's Drag Race: Untucked and RuPaul's Drag Race All Stars: Untucked, according to Deadline. World of Wonder Productions produces all four series.

The renewals arrive as the franchise sits on 11 Emmy nominations this year, including RuPaul Charles' 11th consecutive nod for Outstanding Host for a Reality or Reality Competition Program — a record he extends with each nomination.

Season 18 of the flagship series posted double-digit viewership growth over the prior season and ended with Myki Meeks taking the crown. All Stars Season 11 restructured itself as a Tournament of All Stars, gathering returning queens to compete for a place in the Drag Race Hall of Fame, with Crystal Methyd winning the title.

World of Wonder framed the pickups as a milestone for a show approaching its second decade. "Nearly twenty years later, what began as a dream has become an extraordinary global movement," the company said in a statement, thanking MTV, Paramount+ and "every queen, judge, crew member, and fan who has built RuPaul's Drag Race." The statement added that the company is "honored to keep celebrating new voices and sharing iconic moments with the world."

Neither network has announced premiere dates or casting for the new seasons.

items.title: Dave Marsh, Influential Critic, Activist, Broadcaster & Biographer of Bruce Springsteen, Dies at 76
items.summary:
Dave Marsh, the rock critic, broadcaster and activist who wrote the first book about Bruce Springsteen, died Friday, Aug. 14, at 76. Billboard reported that the cause has not been disclosed, though Marsh had been in declining health for several years.

Born in Pontiac, Michigan, in 1950, Marsh grew up on Motown, R&B and rock 'n' roll, and was among the first editors of Creem when the magazine launched in 1969. He wrote extensively for Rolling Stone and published more than two dozen books, including works on Elvis Presley and The Who. His 1979 Springsteen biography, Born to Run: The Bruce Springsteen Story, became a New York Times bestseller, and in 1993 he shared a Grammy for best album notes for Aretha Franklin's Queen of Soul.

Marsh co-founded the newsletter Rock & Rap Confidential and joined SiriusXM in 2004, hosting Kick Out the Jams for 19 years alongside Live from E Street Nation and Live from the Land of Hope and Dreams. In 2023, an anthology of his work, Kick Out the Jams: Jibes, Barbs, Tributes, and Rallying Cries from 35 Years of Music Writing, drew tributes from Tom Morello, who called him "a tireless advocate of justice, human rights and rock 'n' roll."

Springsteen posted a statement to Instagram on Saturday. "Here on E Street, the irreplaceable loss of Dave Marsh has us heartbroken," he wrote, describing his friend as "soulful, intelligent, heartfelt, opinionated, bruising and often fantastically argumentative," and recalling that watching Marsh and manager Jon Landau argue over obscure records "would make my day." He added, "More than anything else, I admired Dave as a man of conscience and commitment."

Marsh was married to Barbara Carr, Springsteen's longtime co-manager. After the death of their daughter Kristen Ann Carr in 1993, at 21, from sarcoma, he co-founded and served as a trustee of the Kristen Ann Carr Fund, which supports sarcoma research and families affected by cancer.

He was predeceased by daughters Kristen Ann Carr and Sasha Carr, and is survived by his wife. A full list of survivors and service plans had not been released.

items.title: Lisa Knowles-Smith, Darrel Walls & More Win Big at 2026 Stellar Gospel Music Awards: Full Winners List
items.summary:
Lisa Knowles-Smith and Darrel Walls led the winners at the 41st Stellar Gospel Music Awards, taped Saturday, Aug. 15, at the Spectrum Center in Charlotte, North Carolina. Kirk Franklin hosted the ceremony.

Knowles-Smith, 42, took home five trophies, four of them tied to Revival: Live in Dallas, the album she recorded with The Brown Singers. She won the Albertina Walker female artist of the year award, duo/chorus/group of the year and quartet of the year with The Brown Singers, producer of the year with Frederick Perry, and song of the year for "Promises (Live)," credited to her under her legal name, Alescia Knowles-Smith. Billboard reported the song reached No. 5 on its Hot Gospel Songs chart in June.

Walls, 35, won two awards — artist of the year and contemporary male artist of the year — both for Heart of Mine. Vincent Bohanan & SOV won three for Live in New York, including album of the year, contemporary choir of the year, and choir of the year in a tie with JJ Hairston & Youthful Praise. Jonathan McReynolds, John P. Kee, Jekalyn Carr and The Brown Singers each finished with two wins, while Kim Person, who tied Kee with seven nominations apiece, went home empty-handed.

Tasha Cobbs Leonard received the Aretha Franklin Icon Award, and Pastor Mike Jr. was given the Thomas A. Dorsey Most Notable Achievement Award.

The taped show premieres Saturday, Aug. 29, at 8 p.m. ET on The Stellar Network, carried by Charter Spectrum and Verizon Fios, with an encore at 10 p.m. ET. BET airs the national cable premiere Sunday, Aug. 30, at 8 p.m. and 10:30 p.m. ET, followed by broadcast syndication from Sept. 5 through Sept. 27; Bounce TV airs it Sept. 5 at 1 p.m. ET, and WBTV is the local partner in Charlotte. Don Jackson, founder of the Stellar Awards and chairman of Central City Productions, executive produced, with Jennifer J. Jackson as producer and executive in charge of production and Michael A. Johnson producing and directing.

items.title: Selena Gomez’s Attorney Fires Back at Wondermind Lawsuit: “Completely Meritless”
items.summary:
Selena Gomez's attorney has responded to a lawsuit accusing the actor and singer of fraud in connection with Wondermind, the mental health company she co-founded with her mother, Mandy Teefey, and former business partner Daniella Pierson. Litigator Mathew S. Rosengart called the claims against his client baseless and said a motion to dismiss is being filed.

The suit was filed Thursday by two investment vehicles, Wondermind SRS 44 LLC and Bespoke Wondermind SPV LLC, which named Gomez, Teefey and Pierson and allege the founders misrepresented the startup's leadership and its partnerships. The Hollywood Reporter noted the complaint asserts securities fraud, common-law fraud and breach of contract, and seeks rescission of the investment contract along with damages.

Wondermind launched in November 2021 with a focus on what it called mental fitness tools and practices. According to the complaint, investors were told the company would launch an app and benefit from major advertising deals, celebrity photo shoots and magazine cover stories, with Gomez positioned as central to its marketing and Pierson presented as a $200 million executive with a pipeline of revenue-generating initiatives.

"The partnerships did not exist. The initiatives never materialized. The app was never built," the complaint reads, adding that "for three years, while the company quietly collapsed around them, not one of its founders, officers or directors said a word to the investors whose money was funding the collapse."

Rosengart, in a statement to People, said the allegations that Gomez "engaged in any way whatsoever in any purported fraud or other wrongdoing are completely meritless, both factually and legally," and that her team would "vigorously defend these false allegations." A representative for Pierson told USA Today that she denies the claims and welcomes the chance to present documentation and financial records, adding that Pierson invested her own money, took no salary and "has never used investor funds for personal expenses."

items.title: Noah Kahan Brings Chappell Roan on Stage for “California” Performance: Watch
items.summary:
Noah Kahan brought Chappell Roan on stage at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena on Saturday night to perform her song "California." Consequence reported on the appearance, which came late in Kahan's 27-song set on The Great Divide Tour, alongside fan-shot video of the duet.

Kahan introduced the track, from Roan's 2023 debut The Rise and Fall of a Midwest Princess, as the first song of hers he ever heard, and "the reason I fell in love with her." He added that he was "just really proud of her and grateful that she would come sing with me."

Roan used her time at the microphone to return the compliment. "Noah always stands up for me," she told the crowd. "He's a good person, for real."

The Rose Bowl set opened with "American Cars" and closed on "Stick Season," and also featured a second guest, Gigi Perez, on "She Calls Me Back." Kahan's tour continues Monday at Petco Park in San Diego, followed by dates at Chase Field in Phoenix, Oracle Park in San Francisco, America First Field in Sandy, Utah, BC Place in Vancouver and two nights at T-Mobile Park in Seattle.

Roan's next scheduled appearance is at Olivia Rodrigo's Daisy Chain Fields festival on Aug. 29. She has also announced The Super Graphic Spectacular, an October fundraiser for her nonprofit The Midwest Princess Project, which supports LGBTQ+ youth.
